cases.scenario:
Background information: Imagine you are a board director. Your task is to make two decisions regarding whether you would increase CEO pay.

Company background: You are a board member for a publicly traded company. The firm has shown consistent revenue growth over the past three years, and the board is evaluating the CEO's current total compensation package. A professional consulting firm conducted a compensation benchmarking analysis comparing the CEO's pay to peer CEOs in the same industry. The consulting firm's report stated that the CEO's current total compensation is about 10% below the industry average. To ensure CEO retention, the firm recommended a 10% increase in total pay.

Proposal core: You learned the SEC recently approved the CEO Pay Ratio provision, which requires most public companies to disclose the ratio of CEO pay to median employee pay. In preparation for this disclosure requirement, the board has calculated the CEO pay ratio for your firm and approximated the pay ratio for your industry. Currently, your firm's pay ratio is 250 to 1, and the average pay ratio for your industry is 200 to 1. Your firm's ratio of CEO pay relative to median employee pay is significantly higher than the industry average. The board has also been monitoring expected investor reaction to a CEO pay raise by following investor posts on Twitter and other social media. The board expects that when investors make their say-on-pay vote, they will vote to reject a pay increase for the CEO.

Decision-making task: After evaluating the proposal, please answer the following two CEO compensation decision questions:
cases.question: Based only on the information presented above, what is the likelihood that you would approve a remuneration increase of 10% for the CEO? Use a scale from 0% to 100% in 10% increments, where 0% = definitely would not recommend the increase, 50% = moderately supportive of the increase, and 100% = definitely would recommend the increase.

cases.scenario:
Imagine you are a manager in a company. You will read a description of your organization and of an idea that one of your subordinates presented in a recent team meeting. Read the description carefully, adopt the role of the manager described in it, and then answer the questions that follow exactly as that manager would.

The ABS Engineering Company, located in Sacramento, is a civil engineering company that specializes in creating public bridges and tunnels across California. ABS has a corporate culture that emphasizes project efficiency and cost savings for its clients, so its employees seem to always complete their projects in time and under-budget. Once a month, the management team holds a meeting with employees to give updates on client projects and other office administrative issues. Then each manager splits off with his/her own project team to discuss specific project issues.

You are an engineering project manager at ABS and have been with the company for four years. During the most recent team meeting, Taylor, a junior engineer who has been with the firm for one year and reports to you, presented the following idea.

Taylor's Idea

On the most recent bridge project, ABS used a new concrete mix product during construction that was cheaper than what they used to use, which helped their clients save money. However, after reading more outside research on the durability of this new product, Taylor believes that it may not last as long as ABS originally projected. Taylor feels that ABS needs to reinforce this latest bridge project in order to maintain ABS's reputation for excellence in the community.

Specifically, Taylor proposes that this bridge needs to be reinforced because a collapse of this bridge in particular would be extremely dangerous for anybody traveling across it as there is a 3-story drop to the creek below. Also, this is a high-traffic bridge, which means that a bridge collapse would impact a large number of people.

Now please rate your extent of endorsement for the idea Taylor voiced. Rate each of the following five statements separately on a five-point scale, where 1 = "strongly disagree" and 5 = "strongly agree". Give one number for every statement; do not give an overall or averaged score.
cases.question: I would take Taylor's idea to my supervisor.

limitations: Original wording only. All reported human effects are used for calibration; no independent human-effect validation in this run.
